to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2005 ) 

DIMENSIONS FOR SPROCKETS FOR 35 mm MOTION 
PICTURE PROJECTORS 



n 



i. Scope — Dimensions of 16-tooth intermittent sprockets and I6-, 24- and 32-tooth feed and holdback 
sprockets suitable for use with any of the perforations given in iS:608S.|97i 'Dimensions for 35 mm 
motion picture film\ 

2. Terminology 

2.1 Intermittent Sprocket — In intermittently rotating sprocket, usually driven by a Maltese cross device to 
advance the film one frame at a time past the projector aperture at the designated rate. 

2.2 Feed Sprocket — A sprocket serving to draw the film in the direction of rotation; usually applied to a 
sprocket drawing film from a take-off reel. 

2.3 Holdback Sprocket — A sprocket serving to restrain the film against tension: usual^ly applied to a 
sprocket restraining the passage of the film to a take-up reel. 

3. Dimensions and Tooth Forms 

2A The dim.ension of the sprocket shaM be as given below read with the figure. Alternative tooth forms 
are recognized and are designated Type A and Type B in the figure.
